messages:
ravi: Follow-up to RFC: proposing a "service corridor stabilization" playbook focused on long-tail tech debt paydown and clearer ownership for hotpath vs enrichment code. Need quick alignment on guardrails.
sara: love the name. main ask: we need deterministic criteria for when a corridor is 'stable' and pushed to GA.
yuri: agree. suggest three gates: correctness (contract tests pass), performance (p50/p95 within threshold), and operational (observability + rollback tested).avi: Exactly. Draft pass criteria: contract tests green for 3 CI runs, perf p50 <= baseline+5% and p95 <= baseline+20%, and drill for rollback in staging within 10m.
sara: For rollback drills, can we automate a flag flip script? we should rehearse both config rollback and draining canary instances.
yuri: I'll add a small utility that flips routing flags and triggers a graceful drain of the adapter. sample CLI: 
```
# revert corridor routing for tenant
corridorctl rollback --tenant alpha --reason "canary-failure" --timeout 600
```
ops-bot: job scheduled: ci/corridor-rollback-smoke -> staging at 2026-05-01T08:30:00Z
sara: Ownership note: Platform owns corridor runtime and rollout infra; owning teams are responsible for contract tests, migrations, and test data. We should record that in RFC.avi: On tech debt paydown: propose a "stability tax" where new corridor merges must include a plan to remove equivalent functionality from legacy facade or mark feature-flagged TODOs with expiration.
yuri: Good, that prevents indefinite drift. Also add a registry of corridor feature flags with deprecation timestamps.
sara: Monitoring: add these dashboards by default for any corridor: latency histograms, error surface by operation, cache-miss rate, token spend by tenant, and rollback events.avi: Also add a small synthetic traffic job that runs 24/7 in staging to detect regressions early. It should run low-volume but exercise edge cases.
yuri: For KV ownership: hotpath corridor gets co-located KV with low-latency replication; enrichment uses eventual snapshot reads. Migration step: priming job to warm keys before cutover.
sara: Deployment cadence idea: canary (small tenant set) -> 72h shadowing + 24h replay -> gated ramp. All with automatic abort if p95 > threshold or cost guard trips.avi: Cost guard specifics: if incremental token spend > 20% for 30m and not explained by traffic, throttle new corridor to 10% traffic.
yuri: Risks: config sprawl, multi-team coordination, and spurious rollbacks from noisy metrics. Mitigation: central flag store + a lightweight alert suppression window during early canaries.
sara: Final: add a single-line owner field to RFC for each corridor and an escalation matrix. I'll draft the ops playbook and link to RFC.avi: thanks — i'll update RFC with pass criteria, CLI examples, and stability tax. posting link when done. :white_check_mark:
